claim: definition of the benign set B
value: The subset of benign test examples, comprising data that CL did not flag as likely label errors and data that was flagged but for which human reviewers agreed that the original label should be kept.

claim: definition of the unknown-label set U
value: The subset of CL-flagged test examples for which human labelers could not agree on a single correct label. This includes examples where human reviewers agreed that multiple classes or none of the classes are appropriate.

claim: definition of the pruned set P
value: The remaining test data after removing U from D. (P = D \ U)

claim: definition of the correctable set C
value: The subset of CL-flagged examples for which human-validation reached consensus on a different label than the originally given label. (C = P \ B)

claim: how the sets relate
value: B, C, U are disjoint with D = B \cup C \cup U and also P = B \cup C

claim: original accuracy vs corrected accuracy
value: original accuracy: computed with respect to the original labels present in the dataset; corrected accuracy: computed over a modified dataset in which previously identified erroneous labels have been corrected by humans to the true class when possible and removed when not

claim: noise prevalence
value: N = \frac{\vert \mathcal{C} \vert}{\vert \mathcal{P} \vert}

claim: noise prevalence after removing a fraction x of B
value: N = \frac{|\mathcal{C}|}{|\mathcal{P}| - x|\mathcal{B}|}

claim: expected accuracy of model M on the reduced test set
value: A(x; \mathcal{M}) = \frac{A_\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{M}) \cdot |\mathcal{C}| + (1-x) \cdot A_\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{M}) \cdot |B|}{|\mathcal{C}| + (1-x) \cdot |B|}
note: The source writes |B| (not |\mathcal{B}|) for the benign-set size; same set. A_C and A_B are the original or corrected accuracies on C and B before any removal.

claim: A_B does not depend on which labels are used
value: Here A_\mathcal{B} = A_\mathcal{B}^* = \tilde{A}_\mathcal{B} because no erroneous labels were identified in \mathcal{B}.

claim: A(x;M) rewritten as a function of N: a straight line in N
value: A(N) = N \, A_\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{M}) + (1-N) \, A_\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{M})
loc: derived from Sec 5.2 A(x;M) and N = |C|/(|P| - x|B|)
note: Set N = |C|/(|C| + (1-x)|B|); then (1-x)|B|/(|C| + (1-x)|B|) = 1-N, and A(x;M) = N A_C + (1-N) A_B. x = 0 gives N = |C|/|P|; x = 1 gives N = 1 (A = A_C).

claim: noise prevalence at which models 1 and 2 swap rank
value: N^* = \frac{A_\mathcal{B}(1) - A_\mathcal{B}(2)}{(A_\mathcal{B}(1) - A_\mathcal{B}(2)) - (A_\mathcal{C}(1) - A_\mathcal{C}(2))}
note: Solve N A_C(1) + (1-N) A_B(1) = N A_C(2) + (1-N) A_B(2) for N.

claim: how the paper averages over random removals
value: We operationalize averaging over all choices of removal by linearly interpolating from accuracies over the corrected test set (P, with corrected labels for the subset C) to accuracies over the erroneously labeled subset (C, with corrected labels).

claim: the analysis is a lower bound
value: this analysis only presents a loose lower bound on the magnitude of these issues due to unaccounted for label errors in the non-CL-flagged data

claim: recommendation on where to spend annotation budget
value: perhaps by allocating more of an annotation budget to ensure higher quality labels in the test data

claim: closing recommendation
value: We recommend considering the distinction between corrected vs. original test accuracy and curating datasets to maximize high-quality test labels, even if budget constraints only allow for lower-quality training labels.

value: \bar{y}_b=w_b y_b+(1-w_b){p}_{b}
note: p_b = net k's own prediction averaged over M augmentations; w_b from the other net's GMM

claim: Eq 4, temperature sharpening
value: \hat{y}_b=\mathrm{Sharpen}(\bar{y}_b,T)={\bar y_b^c}^{\frac{1}{T}} \bigg/ \sum_{c=1}^C {\bar y_b^c}^{\frac{1}{T}},~\text{for}~ c=1,2,...,C

claim: label co-guessing for unlabeled samples (both nets, all augmentations), then sharpened
value: \bar{q}_{b}=\frac{1}{2M}\sum_{m}\big(\mathrm{p_{model}}(\hat{u}_{b,m};\theta^{(1)})+\mathrm{p_{model}}(\hat{u}_{b,m};\theta^{(2)})\big)
loc: Algorithm 1, line 20 (unnumbered); q_b = Sharpen(q-bar_b, T) on line 21

claim: Eq 6, keep the mix closer to the first sample

value: x'=\lambda' x_1+(1-\lambda')x_2

claim: Eq 8, mixed label
value: p'=\lambda' p_1+(1-\lambda')p_2

claim: Eq 9, cross-entropy on the mixed labeled batch
value: \mathcal{L}_\mathcal{X} = -\frac{1}{|\mathcal{X}'|} \sum_{x,p\in\mathcal{X}'} \sum_{c} p_c \log(\mathrm{p_{model}^c}(x;\theta))

claim: Eq 10, squared error on the mixed unlabeled batch
value: \mathcal{L}_\mathcal{U} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{U}'|} \sum_{x,p\in\mathcal{U}'} \left\lVert {p-\mathrm{p_{model}}(x;\theta)} \right\rVert^2_2

claim: Eq 12, total loss
